source: www/elasticloadbalancing/faqs (snapshot fetched 2026-10-05), plus two guide sentences from docs/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-update-security-groups

d142.note: Duplicates elb-nlb-alb-target-static-ip-privatelink (guide); conflict cf-0372 is a duplicate, not a contradiction. Keep one for teaching, the FAQ one for quick-fire.

d143.note: FAQ 12 and 13 answer with a bare 'Yes.' (schema needs a quote of 8 characters or more), so the facts quote the ALB security-groups guide page.

d145.note: Hypothesis confirmed: no back-end server authentication, only encryption to back ends.

d148.note: FAQ says 'enabled by default' and 'always on'; the user guide says always on at the load balancer level and can be turned off per target group (elb-alb-cross-zone-always-on-lb-level). Not a numeric conflict, so M12 did not queue it: the writer must teach the guide wording and quote the FAQ only for the charge.

d149.not_found: Partial LCUs: FAQ 47 'Will I be billed on partial LCUs?' answers only 'Yes.' (too short to quote; the heading also appears 3 times on the page). Searched snap scope for 'partial LCU': only the FAQ headings. Partial hours are covered by 'each hour or partial hour'.

d151.note: Redirect fact quotes 'three types' and the 'HTTP to HTTPS' line; 'HTTPS to HTTPS' sits 7 lines under the heading (outside the heading-scope window) and is in the packet context only.

d153.note: The FAQ does not say single AZ is 'not recommended' for NLB (it says so for GWLB only).

d155.note: FAQ adds a restriction: PrivateLink cannot be set up with UDP listeners. Check against the PrivateLink guide (chapter 11) before teaching.

d157.note: The NLB FAQ answer does not say 'off by default' (the GWLB answer does); default-off comes from the guide fact elb-nlb-gwlb-cross-zone-off-by-default.

d161.note: The FAQ does not name cross-zone as the fix for an AZ-wide appliance failure; it recommends multiple AZs and scripts that add appliances or send traffic to a GWLB in another AZ.

d165.not_found: The FAQ does not say a GWLB endpoint is a route-table target (hypothesis). Looked in FAQ 125-129. Likely in docs/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-load-balancer-endpoints, section 'Configure routing' (behavior lens).

d166.note: Hypothesis confirmed (750 hours shared). The same FAQ answers say that from July 15, 2025 new customers get up to $200 in Free Tier credits; the 750-hour offer is legacy for new accounts after that date.

faq_vs_guide.issue: FAQ says 200 targets per AZ; the quota page gives a different value. M12 did not pair them (low token overlap): the registrar should open or record the conflict and teach the quota page.
FAQ gives fixed-looking values; the guide has configurable TCP idle timeouts.
FAQ says the timeouts are fixed and cannot be changed; a later change made the GWLB TCP idle timeout configurable. Likely outdated.
FAQ says RSA 2K only, no ECDSA; check the guide, likely outdated.
FAQ says IP targets only for TCP listeners, not UDP; check the guide, likely outdated.
Wording differs (default vs always on at load balancer level, off per target group possible). Not a number conflict.

conflicts_queued.cf-0372: duplicate of a guide fact (same meaning), not a contradiction
conflicts_queued.cf-0383 to cf-0391, cf-0393: false positives: LCU facts of different protocols or load balancer types share words but have different numbers by design; elb-nlb-faq-lcu-tcp/udp/tls repeat the pricing-page NLCU facts (same numbers). Resolve with --both (different scope) or keep only the pricing-page facts.
conflicts_queued.cf-0392: false positive: GWLB vs NLB target limits (different load balancer types)
